summary: The note describes OVATION, a project that aims to create a standard for auroral oval size, position, and precipitation intensity. It provides historical data back to December 1983 and real-time nowcasting, with only University of Alaska, Fairbanks MSP data currently available in real time. Data sets must be long-running and cross-calibrated to previously defined DMSP boundaries, and the project is sponsored by UPOS and supported by NSF grants and research from NSF, AFOSR and NASA.
one_line: OVATION is a project creating a standard for auroral oval size, position and precipitation intensity, with historical and real-time nowcasting data.
key_facts: OVATION stands for Auroral Oval Variation, Assessment, Tracking, Intensity, and Online Nowcasting.
The goal of the OVATION project is to create a "standard" for the auroral oval size, position, and intensity of precipitation.
OVATION includes historical data back to December 1983.
Only data from the University of Alaska, Fairbanks, MSP is currently available in real time.
SuperDARN radar-determined boundaries and other real-time data should soon be included in OVATION.
All data sets incorporated into OVATION must be long-running and cross-calibrated to previously defined DMSP boundaries, using specific procedures.
The OVATION project welcomes additional data sources; contact Patrick Newell or Thomas Sotirelis for more information.
OVATION is sponsored by UPOS (University Partnering for Operational Support).
OVATION includes results of research sponsored by NSF, AFOSR and NASA.
Work on OVATION has been conducted at The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, the University of Alaska, Fairbanks, and the Air Force Research Laboratory.
OVATION is supported by NSF grant ATM-0222411 (P. Newell) and NSF grant ATM-0004365 (T. Sotirelis).
The OVATION page links to pages for plotting historical auroral oval position, viewing real-time plots, data sets, technical background, guidelines, and funding.
